paragraphs.title: Zion’s Light and the Return of Her Children

easy.explanation: Isaiah 60:1 says, “Arise, shine; for thy light is come.”
easy.q: What is Zion told to do?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “the darkness shall cover the earth.”
Verse 3 says, “the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.”
easy.q: Who shall come to Zion’s light?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “thy sons shall come from far.”
medium.q: From where shall Zion’s sons come?

answers: Because the abundance of the sea and the forces of the Gentiles come to her
medium.explanation: Her heart is enlarged because the abundance of the sea and the Gentiles’ forces come to her.
medium.q: Why will Zion’s heart be enlarged?

answers: Zion’s joyful response to the returning people and nations
medium.explanation: Zion sees the gathering people and responds with amazement and joy.
medium.q: What does “flow together” describe in the KJV passage?

challenge.explanation: Darkness covers the earth, but the Lord’s glory rises upon Zion.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears at the beginning of the passage?

answers: Her light draws them to her
They come only because the gates are shut
challenge.explanation: The Gentiles and kings come to Zion’s light and brightness.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Zion’s light and the nations?

answers: Only the return of Zion’s children
The return of her children together with the gathering of nations
challenge.explanation: The passage joins the return of Zion’s sons and daughters with the arrival of nations and their wealth.
challenge.q: Which combination of events is described?

paragraphs.title: The Nations’ Gifts and Sacred Service

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “The multitude of camels shall cover thee.”
Those from Sheba bring “gold and incense.”
easy.q: What shall those from Sheba bring?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions the flocks of Kedar and the rams of Nebaioth.
easy.q: Which animals come from Kedar and Nebaioth?

medium.explanation: They shall “shew forth the praises of the Lord.”
medium.q: What shall those bringing gold and incense show forth?

answers: Minister and come up with acceptance on the altar
medium.explanation: The rams shall minister, and they shall come up with acceptance on the Lord’s altar.
medium.q: What shall the flocks and rams do at Zion?

medium.explanation: A multitude is a large or abundant number.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “multitude” mean?

answers: It is used in sacred service
challenge.explanation: The gifts and animals are connected with worship, the altar, and the glorifying of God’s house.
challenge.q: What does the arrival of the nations’ wealth show about its purpose?

answers: The gifts arrive together with the proclamation of the Lord’s praise
challenge.explanation: Those who bring the gifts also show forth the praises of the Lord.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the nations’ gifts and the Lord’s praise?

answers: The nations approach Zion and serve in holy worship
The wealth of the earth disappears
challenge.explanation: The nations bring wealth and animals that are used in sacred service.

paragraphs.title: Return from Afar and Zion’s Restoration

easy.explanation: They fly “as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows.”
easy.q: To what are those returning to Zion compared?

easy.explanation: The ships come “to bring thy sons from far.”
easy.q: What do the ships of Tarshish bring?

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls.”

answers: By sea and from distant places
medium.explanation: The isles and ships point to the sea, while the people come from far.
medium.q: By what means do people return to Zion in this passage?

medium.explanation: The ships bring Zion’s sons with “their silver and their gold with them.”
medium.q: What do the returning sons bring with them?

answers: Distant lands associated with the sea
medium.explanation: The term refers to distant coastal or sea-associated lands.
medium.q: In the KJV context, what are “the isles”?

challenge.explanation: The image presents the returning people as coming back to their proper home.
challenge.q: What does the comparison to doves returning to their windows emphasize?

answers: They change from enemies or outsiders into builders and partners
They are sent into a new exile
challenge.explanation: They participate in rebuilding Zion’s walls.
challenge.q: How does the role of the sons of strangers change?

challenge.explanation: The returning people and the rebuilt walls together show Zion being restored.
challenge.q: What connects the return of the children with the building of the walls?

paragraphs.title: Open Gates and the Submission of Nations

easy.explanation: The gates “shall be open continually” and shall not be shut day or night.
easy.q: When shall Zion’s gates be open?

easy.explanation: The gates remain open so the forces of the Gentiles may be brought in.
easy.q: What shall the nations bring through the gates?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish.”
easy.q: What will happen to a nation that will not serve Zion?

answers: To beautify the place of the Lord’s sanctuary
medium.explanation: The trees come “to beautify the place of my sanctuary.”
medium.q: Why will the glory of Lebanon come to Zion?

medium.explanation: They come bending and bow themselves at the soles of Zion’s feet.
medium.q: How will those who afflicted Zion come to her?

medium.explanation: Their bent posture shows that they have been humbled.
medium.q: What does “bending” communicate in this context?

answers: The gates are always open, but kingdoms that refuse to serve will perish
The gates are shut while the kingdoms rule
Both the gates and kingdoms disappear
challenge.explanation: Zion welcomes the nations, but refusal to serve brings destruction.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the gates and the kingdoms?

answers: Recognition of Zion’s honored and sacred status
Their desire to destroy the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: They acknowledge Zion as “The city of the Lord” and “The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”
challenge.q: What does the bowing of those who despised Zion demonstrate?

answers: The city of the Lord and the Zion of the Holy One of Israel
The city of the closed gates
challenge.explanation: These titles appear at the end of verse 14.
challenge.q: What name is given to Zion after her transformation?

paragraphs.title: From Exile’s Humiliation to Abundance, Peace, and Salvation

easy.explanation: The Lord says Zion had been “forsaken and hated.”
easy.q: What had Zion been in the past?

answers: An eternal excellency and a joy of many generations
easy.explanation: The Lord will make her “an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.”
Violence, wasting, and destruction will no longer be heard in the land.
easy.q: What will no longer be heard in Zion’s land?

medium.explanation: The poorer materials are replaced with more valuable and excellent ones.
medium.q: What does replacing brass with gold and iron with silver signify?

medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness.”
medium.q: What will characterize Zion’s officers and exactors?

answers: Those who govern or enforce authority
medium.explanation: The word refers to officials or those who exercise authority.
medium.q: In context, what does “exactors” refer to?

answers: A change from abandonment and hatred to abundance, joy, and peace
A change from prosperity to ruin
A change from open gates to exile
challenge.explanation: Zion’s condition is completely transformed from humiliation to glory and security.
challenge.q: What overall process is described in verses 15–18?

challenge.explanation: The Lord says, “thou shalt call thy walls Salvation.”
challenge.q: What is the relationship between salvation and Zion’s walls?

answers: Peace and righteousness without wasting or destruction
challenge.explanation: The passage promises righteous leadership and the removal of violence, wasting, and destruction.
challenge.q: What social condition is promised to Zion?

paragraphs.title: Everlasting Light, a Righteous People, and Hastened Redemption

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light.”
easy.q: Who shall be Zion’s everlasting light?

answers: They will come to an end
easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “the days of thy mourning shall be ended.”
easy.q: What will happen to Zion’s days of mourning?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thy people also shall be all righteous.”

medium.explanation: They “shall inherit the land for ever.”
medium.q: What shall the righteous people inherit?

answers: A little one becomes a thousand and a small one a strong nation
medium.explanation: The final verse describes dramatic growth and strength.
medium.q: How is the growth of the people described?

answers: The Lord will bring it swiftly at the proper time
medium.explanation: The Lord promises to hasten the fulfillment when the appointed time comes.
medium.q: What does “I will hasten it in his time” mean?

answers: The Lord Himself becomes Zion’s everlasting light
There is no light at all
challenge.explanation: The Lord replaces the sun and moon as the source of Zion’s everlasting light.
challenge.q: How does the light in these verses differ from ordinary daylight?

answers: The righteous people shall inherit the land forever
challenge.explanation: The people are described as righteous, and they shall inherit the land forever.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between righteousness and inheritance?

answers: He will hasten the fulfillment at the proper time
He will stop the growth of the people
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends with the promise, “I the Lord will hasten it in his time.”
challenge.q: How is the Lord’s action described at the end of the chapter?
